steps.title: Look at the three sentences again.
steps.sub: … is a round box. · The box is called … · It contains — personal things.
steps.prompt: Why does the speaker say a round box first, and the box after that?
options: The first time is new information; after that we both know which box.
Because the box is round and not square like the others.
Because the second sentence is longer than the first one.
steps.answer: The first time is new information; after that we both know which box.
steps.why: A / an introduces something new; the is for something we have already met or can both identify.

steps.title: a / an, the, and no article
steps.html:
ArticleUse it forExample
a / anone of many, first mentionIt’s a metal ball.
a / ana job or what something isShe’s an architect.
thewe both know which oneThe box does not close.
thethere is only onethe sun, the internet, the seafront
thewith a superlativeIt’s the heaviest of the five.
—things in general (plural)Possessions are about time.
—uncountable things in generalIt’s made of metal.

Use an before a vowel sound: an antique ring, an hour — but a university, because it begins with a /j/ sound.

Say the when the listener can already work out which one you mean — from the situation, or because you said it before.

Use no article for plural and uncountable nouns when you mean them in general: I like books. It’s made of leather.

The most common mistake is dropping a before a job: say She’s a nurse, not She’s nurse.

How much and how many of something — that is the next lesson.

steps.title: Five objects, one person
steps.sub: Five objects went into the car. Everything else went away.
steps.html:
Reading

When Aigerim moved flat she gave away almost everything. Five objects went into the car.

The first is a wooden box the size of a book. Her father made it in 1994. The lid does not close properly and there is nothing inside it, but it is the only thing she has from that year.

The second is a cheap steel watch. It is not valuable — she bought it in a market for the price of two coffees — but it was on her wrist during three job interviews, and she passed all three. “I don’t believe in luck,” she says. “I just like the watch.”

The third is a pair of leather gloves, dark brown and very thin. Her grandmother wore them for thirty winters. They are too small for Aigerim, so she keeps them in a drawer.

The fourth is not one object but a collection: forty-one postcards from people who are no longer in her life. She reads them once a year, in January.

The fifth is the heaviest and the strangest: a round metal ball she found on a beach when she was nine. Nobody knows what it is. It is bright in one place where she rubbed it as a child.

“People think possessions are about money,” she says. “Most of mine cost nothing. They are about time.”

steps.title: Choose the best answer.
steps.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
options: The objects she kept are about time, not about money.
She kept the five most expensive things she owned.
She regrets giving so many things away.
steps.answer: The objects she kept are about time, not about money.
steps.why: “Most of mine cost nothing. They are about time.”
